evidence: src/pool.ts:1071 PORCELAIN_LINE_BEFORE_Z accepts any line that begins 'worktree ', 'HEAD ', 'branch ', 'locked ' or 'prunable ', so the newline fallback (git before 2.36, where `worktree list` has no -z) cannot tell a path's second line from a new record. `currentPath` is the LAST 'worktree ' line before the 'branch' line (src/pool.ts:1205-1207), so a foreign worktree whose path ends in '<LF>worktree <own worktree path>' is read as the task's own worktree and never refuses.

MEASURED on git 2.34.1 (git_2.34.1-1ubuntu1.17_amd64.deb, sha256 8794fcf2..., extracted to scratch and run through a wrapper, never installed), node v26.6.0, head 0027bbb, dist built, real `tiphys init`, `pool create --task t-old`, `git checkout --detach` in the pool worktree, then `git worktree add --force "$T/x<LF>worktree $T/fleet/worktrees/t-old" task/t-old` (script scratchpad/rev-c/p/pooldestroy.sh, arm 2.34-crafted): `pool destroy --task t-old` exit 0, stdout 'destroyed t-old (deleted branch task/t-old was f238164a...)', branch GONE while the foreign worktree still had it checked out. SAME FIXTURE on git 2.43.0 (the -z arm) exit 1 'cannot delete branch task/t-old: it is checked out at <tmp>/x<LF>worktree <own>; remove that worktree first', branch present.

CONTROLS on 2.34.1, same script: a foreign path with a space, a TAB, a backslash plus double quote, or a non-ASCII byte all refuse with 'it is checked out at ...' (git 2.34.1 prints these raw, not quoted); a foreign path '<dir>/fo<LF>reign' refuses with the new 'printed "reign", which is no attribute' line. So only a path whose continuation line itself starts with an attribute keyword passes.

The work history records this shape as not constructed (Fix round 4, 'What the derivations did not cover', 'A worktree path whose continuation after a newline itself begins worktree , HEAD ...'). It is now constructed and it passes.
findings.concrete-fix: Validate the newline listing by RECORD grammar instead of per-line prefix. Split on blank lines; each record must be exactly one 'worktree ' line, then 'bare' or ('HEAD ' then 'branch ' or 'detached'), then optional 'locked'/'locked <reason>'/'prunable <reason>' lines, and nothing else; a second 'worktree ' line inside a record or a record with no HEAD/bare makes the listing unreadable (the existing worktreeListError refusal); apply the same grammar to the -z listing (split on NUL, records end at an empty field) so both forms share one validator. Add the crafted path as a fourth arm of the 'worktree listing cannot be read' test, replaying git 2.34.1's real newline listing of it (record it with the same capture script).
findings.analysis: Low because the trigger is a deliberately crafted path that embeds the literal text of the task's own worktree path after a newline: no accident produces it, anyone able to create that worktree already has command execution in the repository, and destroy without --delete-branch-force still requires the branch tip to equal its recorded base, so no commit is lost by default. It is a guard that passes while its subject is broken on git 2.34.1, which is why it is recorded.

evidence: test/pool.test.ts:431-433 (replayWorktreeListing) re-runs the capture's `git worktree list --porcelain -z` live as its anchor before destroy runs, so the round-3 test 'pool destroy refuses while a foreign worktree at the task's own path plus a newline holds the task branch' needs git 2.36 or later by itself, although the product behaviour it guards (destroy on a newline path) is supported on older git by the round-4 fallback.

MEASURED: full suite `node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"` at head 0027bbb, node v26.6.0, git 2.34.1 first on PATH, dist built: tests 1244, pass 1232, fail 12 (scratchpad/rev-c/suite-git234.log). The same suite files at base a726478 on git 2.34.1 fail 11 (test/doctor.test.ts 1, test/next.test.ts 4, test/teardown.test.ts 6, each of which also fails at head); the twelfth failure at head is this test, 'AssertionError: git git worktree list --porcelain -z: error: unknown switch `z'' from the anchor, not from destroy. test/pool.test.ts at base: 42 tests, 42 pass on 2.34.1; at head 45 tests, 44 pass.

Every other test of rounds 1 to 4 passes on git 2.34.1, including the five round-4 tests (pool z-fallback, unread listing, quoted-TAB header, credential probes, doctor retention) and the round-3 -z tests for scope, cutover, witness and gates.
findings.concrete-fix: Make the anchor version-aware: skip the live `-z` comparison (keep the stderr/exit assertion from the capture) when `git worktree list --porcelain -z` itself exits 129 with the unknown-switch line, or record a second capture case for git before 2.36 and compare against that one. The test's destroy assertions need no change.
findings.analysis: Low: the repository declares no git floor, `npm test` already fails on git 2.34.1 at the base (11 tests), and CI runs a newer git. Recorded because it is one more test that cannot pass on the oldest git the fix round itself targets.

evidence: src/pool.ts:1205-1224 (resolveDestroy) reads a SUCCESSFUL but empty or unrecognisable listing as 'no other worktree holds the branch': with `-z` (git 2.36 and later, every current git) the lines are never validated, so stdout with no 'worktree ' record at all leaves branchCheckedOutAt undefined and stage 3 deletes the branch. Only the newline fallback checks its lines (PORCELAIN_LINE_BEFORE_Z, src/pool.ts:1071).

MEASURED on git 2.43.0 (node v26.6.0, head 0027bbb, dist built, real CLI; scratchpad/rev-c/p/pooldestroy.sh with GITBIN=scratchpad/rev-c/p/emptywrap): a `git` wrapper first on PATH that exits 0 with no output for any `... list` invocation and execs /usr/bin/git otherwise, a foreign worktree holding task/t-old: `pool destroy --task t-old` exit 0 'destroyed t-old (deleted branch task/t-old was fb490737...)', branch GONE. Control, real git, same fixture: exit 1 'cannot delete branch task/t-old: it is checked out at <tmp>/for eign'.

This is the empty-output sibling of the round-3 regression (a listing read only when it succeeded, an absent reading taken as the harmless one): round 4 closed the failed-exit arm and the unreadable-newline arm and left the successful-but-empty arm.
findings.concrete-fix: In worktreeListLines, require at least one 'worktree ' record in the listing of either form (git always lists the main worktree or the bare repository), and otherwise return { ok: false, detail: 'git worktree list printed no worktree record' } so evaluateDestroy refuses through the existing worktreeListError path. Add the wrapper as a fourth arm of the 'worktree listing cannot be read' test.
findings.analysis: Low: no git prints an empty successful listing, so the trigger is a non-conforming git shim or a truncated pipe that still exits 0. Recorded because the brief names an empty output as a fail-open read and this destroy guard is the only thing standing between update-ref and a checked-out branch.

Only `worktree list -z` is newer than git 2.34.1 (it arrived in 2.36): ran it on git 2.34.1 (Ubuntu 22.04 deb, sha256 8794fcf2..., extracted to scratch through a wrapper, never installed; `worktree list --porcelain -z` exit 129 'error: unknown switch `z'', the text src/pool.ts:1061 matches and witness/captures/m6-p3-git-worktree-list-z.json records).
